title: The Spirit of Solomon
subtitle: What is Love To A Man Made To Destroy It

samplePoems.title: Rise
samplePoems.content:
They called me wise before I learned
what wisdom cost—
before the gold turned cold
in hands that held too much.

I built kingdoms on foundations
of borrowed time,
thought I could master
what was meant to humble me.

But every crown weighs heavy
on a head that knows
the price of being loved
for what you own.

samplePoems.title: The Weight of Choosing
samplePoems.content:
Between right and easy,
I chose comfort.
Between truth and peace,
I chose silence.

Now I sit in the ruins
of my careful compromises,
wondering if wisdom
was always meant to hurt this much.

Solomon had his temple;
I have my lessons,
both built from stones
of what we thought we knew.

samplePoems.title: What Remains
samplePoems.content:
When the last applause fades,
when the crowds disperse,
when the mirrors show
only the man beneath the myth—

what remains?

Not the gold or glory,
not the songs they sang,
but the quiet truth
that love was always
the only currency that mattered.

And I spent it all
on things that couldn't love me back.

description: A confession in verse tracing the rise and fall of a man who believed he could have it all without paying the price.

title: Our Father?
subtitle: A Poetic Journey Through Faith, Doubt, and Divine Silence

samplePoems.title: Questions in the Dark
samplePoems.content:
Our Father, who art in heaven—
or so they tell me.
But where were you
when the prayers felt like
shouting into an empty room?

Hallowed be thy name,
though I struggle to say it
when doubt sits heavy
on my tongue
like communion bread
that won't dissolve.

I'm still here,
still speaking to the silence,
still hoping
you're listening
from wherever
fathers go
when their children
need them most.

samplePoems.title: Divine Silence
samplePoems.content:
They say you work in mysterious ways,
but mystery feels a lot like absence
when you're seventeen
and the world is burning
and you can't find your voice
in the choir of certainty.

Maybe silence is an answer.
Maybe waiting is worship.
Maybe faith was never
meant to be comfortable,
never meant to fit
in the boxes we build
for things we think we understand.

So I'll sit in the questions,
make peace with the unknown,
and call this prayer too.

samplePoems.title: Still Searching
samplePoems.content:
I used to know you
in Sunday morning songs,
in stained glass stories,
in the easy answers
of childhood faith.

Now I look for you
in the spaces between words,
in the hurt that teaches,
in the love that stays
even when belief falters.

Our Father,
whoever you are,
wherever you are,
I'm still your child,
still searching,
still hoping
that the questions
are prayers too,
and that seeking
is its own form
of finding.

description: A candid wrestling with prayer and presence—when belief collides with unanswered questions.

title: Poems from a Black Boy
subtitle: Identity, Heritage, and Hope

samplePoems.title: Morning Mirrors
samplePoems.content:
I wake up Black
every morning,
check the mirror
to make sure
it's still me
looking back.

Some days I see my father's strength,
my mother's grace,
my grandmother's wisdom
woven into the curve
of my smile,
the fire in my eyes.

Other days I see the weight
of expectations,
the burden of representation,
the beautiful responsibility
of carrying ancestors' dreams
in every step I take.

But every morning,
I choose to see
not just survival,
but the art
of becoming
who I was meant to be.

samplePoems.title: Heritage
samplePoems.content:
They tried to erase us
from textbooks,
redline us out of neighborhoods,
code-switch us
into silence.

But we are the children
of people who turned
scraps into feasts,
songs into resistance,
pain into power.

We carry kingdoms
in our DNA,
carry rhythms
older than oppression,
carry light
that no darkness
can diminish.

I am not broken.
I am not angry.
I am not less than.

I am heir
to a legacy
of overcomers,
and their strength
runs through my veins
like liquid gold.

samplePoems.title: Future Tense
samplePoems.content:
To the Black boys
who come after me:

You are not a statistic.
You are not a threat.
You are not less than
what they see
when they look at you
with fear in their eyes.

You are possibility.
You are brilliance.
You are the answer
to prayers your ancestors
whispered in the dark.

Wear your skin
like the crown it is.
Speak your truth
like the prophecy it is.
Love yourself
like the revolution it is.

The world is waiting
for what only you
can give it.

Don't keep us waiting
too long.

description: Raw, unfiltered verse on belonging, history, and the beauty found in surviving and becoming.

title: Hopeless Romantic
subtitle: Love, Loss, and Everything Between

samplePoems.title: First Love
samplePoems.content:
You were my first lesson
in what it means
to give someone else
the power to make
or break your day
with just a text message.

I wrote your name
in the margins
of math notebooks,
practiced saying
'I love you'
in the mirror
until it sounded
less like a prayer
and more like a promise.

You taught me that hearts
can hold infinite love
and infinite pain
at the exact same time,
that seventeen
is old enough
to know forever
and young enough
to believe in it.

Thank you
for being my first
everything,
even the first
to teach me
how to let go.

samplePoems.title: After You
samplePoems.content:
I'm learning to love
the sound of my own laugh
without waiting
for your approval.

I'm learning to make plans
without checking
if you're free first,
to eat at restaurants
we never went to together,
to listen to songs
that don't remind me
of what we used to be.

Slowly, carefully,
I'm becoming someone
who doesn't need you
to feel complete,
though I'm grateful
for the time
when I did.

Love taught me
how to open.
Loss is teaching me
how to close
the things that need closing,
how to keep open
the things worth keeping.

I'm keeping the way
you made me believe
I was worthy of love.
I'm closing the door
on needing you
to prove it.

samplePoems.title: Hope is a Dangerous Thing
samplePoems.content:
Hope is a dangerous thing
for someone like me,
someone who falls
in love with possibilities,
who sees forever
in a first kiss,
who writes wedding vows
after a second date.

But I'd rather be
hopeless romantic
than hopeless cynic,
rather believe too much
than believe too little,
rather risk heartbreak
than risk never feeling
the particular magic
of loving someone
so completely
that their happiness
becomes your religion.

So yes,
I'll keep believing
in love at first sight,
in soulmates,
in happily ever after,
in the kind of love
that writes itself
into poetry.

Because hope
is the only thing
more dangerous
than love itself—
and I'm addicted
to both.

description: An intimate, emotionally charged collection on longing, closure, and the courage to stay tender.

title: Boys Raised in Silence
subtitle: Breaking the Quiet, Finding Voice

samplePoems.title: The Quiet
samplePoems.content:
We were taught to swallow pain
like bitter medicine,
to smile through the ache,
to carry burdens
that would break men twice our size.

Silence was strength,
they said.
Tears were weakness.
Vulnerability was surrender.

So we learned to hide
behind masks of toughness,
buried our emotions
in unmarked graves,
built walls so high
even we forgot
what we were protecting.

But silence doesn't heal wounds.
It just lets them fester
in the dark.

samplePoems.title: Breaking Point
samplePoems.content:
There comes a moment
when the weight becomes too much,
when the mask cracks,
when the walls crumble,
when silence
finally screams.

For me, it was midnight,
alone in my room,
realizing that strength
isn't about holding it all in—
it's about having the courage
to let it out.

To speak.
To cry.
To ask for help.
To admit
that I'm not okay,
and that's okay.

samplePoems.title: Voice
samplePoems.content:
They tried to silence us
with expectations,
with stereotypes,
with the weight
of what it means
to be a man.

But our voices
were always there,
waiting beneath the surface,
ready to rise.

Now I speak
not just for myself,
but for every boy
who was told to be quiet,
every man
who learned too late
that vulnerability
is not the opposite of strength—
it's the foundation.

description: A powerful exploration of the cost of silence and the courage required to speak your truth as a young Black man.

title: The Adventures of Kiminou the Great and Chua the Wise
subtitle: A Journey of Friendship and Discovery

samplePoems.title: The Beginning
samplePoems.content:
In a land where stories bloom like flowers,
where wisdom grows on ancient trees,
two friends embarked on a journey
that would change everything.

Kiminou the Great,
with courage in his heart
and dreams too big for one world,
met Chua the Wise,
who saw the truth
in every shadow,
heard the lesson
in every silence.

Together, they learned
that greatness and wisdom
are not opposites—
they are partners
on the path to becoming.

samplePoems.title: The Lesson of the Mountain
samplePoems.content:
Kiminou wanted to climb the highest peak,
to plant his flag at the summit,
to prove his greatness to the world.

But Chua said,
'The mountain does not need you
to climb it.
It simply is.
Perhaps the lesson
is not in conquering,
but in appreciating.
Not in reaching the top,
but in honoring the journey.'

And Kiminou learned
that true greatness
isn't about being seen—
it's about seeing clearly.

samplePoems.title: The Gift of Friendship
samplePoems.content:
They say you cannot choose your family,
but you can choose your friends.

Kiminou and Chua chose each other,
not because they were alike,
but because they were different—
different in all the right ways.

One saw adventure where the other saw caution.
One saw possibility where the other saw danger.
One rushed forward while the other paused to think.

And together,
they were unstoppable,
balanced,
complete.

Because the greatest adventures
are always better
when shared with someone
who helps you see
what you couldn't see alone.

description: A whimsical tale of two friends learning that courage and wisdom work best together on life's greatest adventures.

title: Black Boy Poems
subtitle: Poems from the Weight of Black Boyhood
description: An unflinching collection tracing Black boyhood through identity, silence, trauma, and the unbreakable pursuit of joy.

title: Kiminou's World of Imagination: The Basics
subtitle: A Colorful Journey Through Imagination and Play
description: A children's book about imagination, play, and the power of believing in what you can build.
